subject: music
title: Interval Identification
welcome_lead: P5, m3, M3, P4 — the building blocks of melody.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: identifying intervals by ear.
final_note: Train the ear, name the interval.

concepts.def: 7 semitones — e.g. C to G; 'Twinkle, twinkle'.
4 semitones — e.g. C to E; 'When the Saints'.
5 semitones — e.g. C to F; 'Amazing Grace'.

walkthroughs.body_html: Aural reference: P5 = Twinkle Twinkle; P4 = Amazing Grace; M3 = When the Saints; m3 = Greensleeves; M6 = NBC chimes; tritone = Maria from West Side Story.
Practise ascending and descending separately. A descending m6 sounds like 'Love Story'; ascending m6 like the opening of The Entertainer's bridge.

mcqs.q: C to G is which interval?
A tritone spans how many semitones?
How many semitones are in a perfect fifth?
How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Perfect Fifth (P5)”?
options: 4 semitones — e.g. C to E; 'When the Saints'.
7 semitones — e.g. C to G; 'Twinkle, twinkle'.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Major Third (M3)”?
options: 4 semitones — e.g. C to E; 'When the Saints'.
5 semitones — e.g. C to F; 'Amazing Grace'.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Perfect Fourth (P4)”?
options: 7 semitones — e.g. C to G; 'Twinkle, twinkle'.
5 semitones — e.g. C to F; 'Amazing Grace'.
4 semitones — e.g. C to E; 'When the Saints'.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Interval”?
options: 7 semitones — e.g. C to G; 'Twinkle, twinkle'.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Minor Third (m3)”?
options: 5 semitones — e.g. C to F; 'Amazing Grace'.
4 semitones — e.g. C to E; 'When the Saints'.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Tritone”?
options: 4 semitones — e.g. C to E; 'When the Saints'.
7 semitones — e.g. C to G; 'Twinkle, twinkle'.

12 semitones (e.g. C-C) — the widest interval in this list
